Project: PostgreSQL. Upgrade being assessed: 13 -> 16.
This change was introduced in release 15. Source: PostgreSQL 15 release notes: Migration to Version 15 (official_release_notes). Section: Release 15 / Migration to Version 15.
Version facts from package metadata for this release (authoritative for version numbers): none

ITEM:
<<<
Remove server-side language plpython2u and generic Python language plpythonu (Andres Freund) Python 2.x is no longer supported. While the original intent of plpythonu was that it could eventually refer to plpython3u, changing it now seems more likely to cause problems than solve them, so it's just been removed.
>>>

PARENT CONTEXT (same section, for disambiguation only):
<<<
Release 15 / Migration to Version 15: A dump/restore using pg_dumpall or use of pg_upgrade or logical replication is required for those wishing to migrate data from any previous release. See upgrading for general information on migrating to new major releases. Version 15 contains a number of changes that may affect compatibility with previous releases. Observe the following incompatibilities: Remove PUBLIC creation permission on the public schema (Noah Misch) The new default is one of the secure schema usage patterns that ddl-schemas-patterns has recommended since the security release for CVE-2018-1058. The change applies to new database clusters and to newly-created databases in existing clusters. Upgrading a cluster or restoring a database dump will preserve public's existing permissions. For existing databases, especially those having multiple users, consider revoking CREATE permission on the public schema to adopt this new default. For new databases having no need to defend against insider threats, granting CREATE permission will yield the behavior of prior releases. Change the owner of the public schema to be the new pg_database_owner role (Noah Misch) This allows each database's owner to have ownership privileges on the public schema within their database. Previously it was owned by the bootstrap superuser, so that non-superuser database owners could not do anything with it. This change applies to new database clusters and to newly-created databases in existing clusters. Upgrading a cluster or restoring a database dump will preserve public's existing ownership specification. Remove long-deprecated exclusive backup mode (David Steele, Nathan Bossart) If the database server stops abruptly while in this mode, the server could fail to start. The non-exclusive backup mode is considered superior for all purposes. Functions pg_start_backup()/pg_stop_backup() have been renamed to pg_backup_start()/pg_backup_stop(), and the functions pg_backup_start_time() and pg_is_in_backup() have been removed. Increase hash_mem_multiplier default to 2.0 (Peter Geoghegan) This allows query hash operations to use more work_mem memory than other operations. Remove server-side language plpython2u and generic Python language plpythonu (Andres Freund) Python 2.x is no longer supported. While the original intent of plpythonu was that it could eventually refer to plpython3u, changing it now seems more likely to cause problems than solve them, so it's just been removed. Generate an
>>>

Decide the disposition:
- "risk": the item describes something that can break an app/deployment, require migration work, or create operational risk.
- "context": it is accurate but needs no action at 16 (no user action required, deprecated-but-working, additive feature). Give the reason.

For "risk", produce one or more risk paths. Use separate paths for separate symbols/APIs when they can be checked independently. Hard rules:
1. Every condition has at least one quote copied EXACTLY, character for character, from ITEM or PARENT CONTEXT (contiguous span, 3-40 words, no ellipses, no added words). Do not fix typos or formatting.
2. Each path has exactly one condition with category "version" stating that the upgrade crosses release 15 (quote the text that ties the change to this release, or the change statement itself), and at least one application/deployment condition (category api_usage, configuration, dependency, runtime, deployment, database, behavior or test_coverage) describing what the app or deployment must use/have for the risk to apply.
3. If the text does not state something you need, do not assert it: use role "uncertain" and explain in ambiguities. derived_by: "extraction" when the text states the fact; for an application/deployment condition ("the application uses X"), use "extraction" when the text names X as the thing affected by the change. Use "inference" only when you infer an affected symbol, scope or impact that the text does not name. Only add ambiguities for real gaps or conflicts in the text, not for the general fact that a specific application has not been inspected.
4. role: "required" (must hold), "alternative" (any one of the alternatives suffices), "optional" (raises impact), "disqualifying" (if it holds, the risk does NOT apply, e.g. not using the new opt-in API), "uncertain".
5. operator/expected_value must be checkable: e.g. operator "present" with expected_value the literal symbol; "less_than" with a version; "equals" with a setting value. expected_value is a string.
6. If a replacement API/setting/version is named, put the migration step in suggested_actions and add a condition for any behavior that differs in the replacement when the text states one.
7. search_queries: for app-side conditions with a literal symbol, give ripgrep regexes (tool "ripgrep"), kubectl commands (tool "kubectl") or SQL (tool "sql") that would find usage. Empty list if no literal symbol.
8. primary_symbol: the most specific identifier of the change (full apiVersion string like "policy/v1beta1", setting name, function, flag, or runtime name like "Python"/"Node.js"). symbols: all identifiers involved.
9. risk_level rubric: critical = upgrade fails or data is at risk for most users meeting the conditions (e.g. unsupported runtime/database version, removed API version that stops serving); high = code or config meeting the conditions breaks at upgrade; medium = behavior change or migration with a clear workaround; low = edge case, cosmetic, or warning-only.
10. fires_at: "upgrade" (at upgrade time), "first_use" (when a feature is first exercised), "rotation" (on credential/password rotation), "rollout" (on deployment rollout), "future_removal" (deprecated now, removed later).
11. applies_to: fill upgrade_method (e.g. "pg_upgrade", "dump/restore"), cluster_type, or from_versions (a version specifier like "<3.1") ONLY if the text restricts applicability; otherwise null.
Do not output confidence.

paths.description: PostgreSQL 15 removes the server-side language plpython2u; Python 2.x is no longer supported. Functions and extensions written in plpython2u will not work after upgrading from 13 to 16.

conditions.statement: Upgrade crosses PostgreSQL release 15, where plpython2u was removed
quotes: Remove server-side language plpython2u and generic Python language plpythonu
conditions.relevance: Removal happened in release 15; the 13 -> 16 upgrade crosses it.

conditions.statement: The database has the plpython2u language installed or functions written in plpython2u
conditions.relevance: Objects using this language will break after upgrade.

search_queries.query: SELECT lanname FROM pg_language WHERE lanname = 'plpython2u';
SELECT p.oid::regprocedure FROM pg_proc p JOIN pg_language l ON p.prolang = l.oid WHERE l.lanname = 'plpython2u';

suggested_actions: Find all functions and extensions using plpython2u and port them to Python 3 under plpython3u before upgrading.
Drop the plpython2u language/extension from the old cluster once migrated.

paths.description: PostgreSQL 15 removes the generic Python language plpythonu. It was not changed to point to plpython3u; it was simply removed, so objects using plpythonu will break.

conditions.statement: Upgrade crosses PostgreSQL release 15, where plpythonu was removed
quotes: Remove server-side language plpython2u and generic Python language plpythonu
conditions.relevance: Removal happened in release 15; the 13 -> 16 upgrade crosses it.

conditions.statement: The database has the plpythonu language installed or functions or DDL scripts using LANGUAGE plpythonu
conditions.relevance: plpythonu no longer exists and is not aliased to plpython3u.

search_queries.query: SELECT lanname FROM pg_language WHERE lanname = 'plpythonu';
SELECT p.oid::regprocedure FROM pg_proc p JOIN pg_language l ON p.prolang = l.oid WHERE l.lanname = 'plpythonu';

conditions.statement: plpythonu was not redirected to plpython3u; it was removed
quotes: changing it now seems more likely to cause problems than solve them, so it's just been removed
conditions.relevance: Code relying on plpythonu becoming an alias for plpython3u will fail.

suggested_actions: Rewrite functions and DDL scripts using LANGUAGE plpythonu to use plpython3u, porting any Python 2 code to Python 3.
Remove plpythonu from the old cluster before upgrading.
